punchline: When Melville knew readers would laugh at a whale sinking a ship, he gave them a witness: the Essex.
thirty_sec: In Moby-Dick, Melville stops the story for a chapter called The Affidavit. He knows people ashore think a whale sinking a ship is a joke, so he cites the Essex of Nantucket, quotes first mate Owen Chase's narrative, and says he has spoken with Chase's son. Then he adds a second case, the Union, and admits he has never found the details. He backs his claim with witnesses and tells you which one is weak.
